Easy Mode Priority Rotation

 Arcane Barrage if you run out of mana
 
Below here you'll find a more in-depth presentation of the rotation, opener, and details on why we do what we do.

Arcane Mage Rotation in 

Arcane Mage ultimately plays around 2 primary resources, Mana and Arcane Charge s and 2 secondary resources, Arcane Salvo and our cooldowns and much of what pushes and pulls us in our rotation are driven by these 4 resources. This sounds complex, but once you practice the spec these concepts quickly become intuitively related and second nature. Breaking down each of these:

 

 

 
 Mana Management: This is something many newer players struggle with, however it is important you remember going out of mana is perfectly fine, especially after your miniburn. Simply use Arcane Barrage to clear your Arcane Charge s which throttles your mana spend and continue with the rotation. Mana problems can be tilting, but we are a cooldown-based spec first and our main cooldowns give us all the mana we need for those windows. Just remember to breathe when you run out of mana; Barrage and move on!
 

 

 
 

 
 Arcane Charges: Arcane Charge s are generated by Arcane Blast , Arcane Explosion , Arcane Pulse , Arcane Orb , Touch of the Magi , and lastly when talented into High Voltage . The only ways to clear them is Arcane Barrage , Arcane Missiles with the talent Charged Missiles or waiting around while out of combat; spending charges with Barrage makes it hit harder and cleave. Arcane Charges increase the mana cost of Blast and Pulse and their damage. This creates a loop where you want to use Barrage to reduce the mana spend at times so you can ensure a successful Miniburn. Take your time and build muscle memory for the relationship your spells have with Arcane Charge generation. In AOE the opposite is often true where you usually want to get 4 Arcane Charges and then Barrage, that said this is weighed against the next resource.
 

 

 
 

 
 Arcane Salvo: Arcane Salvo is fairly straight-forward, usually using Arcane Barrage at max stacks or in conjunction with a way to quickly refund Salvo stacks or Arcane Charges. There are a lot of ways that Salvo interacts with each hero talent and our spells and abilities and as such you should definitely spend the time to read those talents and understand the interactions as they will be relevant later on. Remember you can use the search function in the talent system to identify the talents that actually interact with Salvo!
 

 

 
 

 
 Don't Sit on Cooldowns: Arcane Surge gives us a huge refund on mana on top of the damage increase and other effects for the hero talents. This means holding this cooldown essentially tanks other aspects of the rotation, causing us to run out of mana more frequently, Barrage more without Salvo, causing a cascade of failures downstream in our potential damage. Our cooldowns are also short and on a low cooldown. it is almost always better to squeeze in as many as you can over the course of a fight or dungeon. That said, don't be afraid to volunteer to hold cooldowns for a specific problem in an encounter, as one of the strengths of short cooldowns is to provide targeted damage when you need it most without losing many uses. But as I said above with regards to mana management, your cooldowns are what give you mana to play with and also make that mana worth more, make sure you're using them as much as possible to fuel the arcane engine!

What makes this builds distinct? Simply put, Orb Build runs Orb Mastery and Missile Build runs High Voltage . These talents essentially cause Arcane Orb and Arcane Missiles to cover the other's effect in our rotation (generating Arcane Salvo and Arcane Charge s).

Pre-Combat Check

Before any combat happens, it is important for Arcane Mages to make sure the following steps are checked. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content, these are the things that keep you powerful, make a habit of just using them when out of combat all the time!

 Arcane Mage Major Cooldowns

Arcane only has a few cooldowns, Arcane Surge , Touch of the Magi , and Evocation . Below are some considerations when using these:

 Arcane Surge

 Arcane Surge is simple, you use it, it spends all of your mana, does a burst of damage that hits 5 targets, then square root damage beyond that. Arcane Surge then buffs you for 15-seconds, granting 35% additional spell damage and 425% mana regen. There are other properties of this that come from hero talents.

Spellslinger changes Arcane Surge in one major way, Splinterstorm in Midnight causes your Surge hit to generate 8x Arcane Splinter s and doubles Splinter generation during its buff; Archmage's Wrath also buffs Surge damage a decent chunk. Keep in mind that Splinters for Spellslinger are fuel for the fire, it's what makes Spellslinger work.

Sunfury has a few ways that it alters Arcane Surge . First, when you cast Surge, any Spellfire Spheres you have are consumed and added to your Surge buff for the duration of Surge. Second, when Surge ends, you gain Arcane Soul and Ashes of Inspiration , enabling a powerful burst of damage, ultimately extending your burst window; there is also a talent, though we won't take it for now, that can extend Surge's window a couple seconds. Arcane Soul is a major reason why we cast Touch of the Magi late in our Surge window as Sunfury. Lastly, when you cast Surge, you spawn an Arcane Phoenix , which, for every Spellfire Sphere you consumed, cast empowered spells and the bird will also cast regular spells too. The bird is really complex in how it works, it detects whether it's single target or AOE and has a different action list based on this, it can cast it's own version of the following spells:
 
 Empowered Abilities 

 Arcane Surge 

 Greater Pyroblast 

 Meteorite 

 Single Target 

 Arcane Barrage 

 Pyroblast 

 Meteorite 

 AOE 

 Meteorite 

 Flamestrike 

 Arcane Barrage 
 
None of this is really important, it's just cool to know.

 Touch of the Magi 

 Touch of the Magi is a great nuke, but it has a few caveats in how to use it. First, Touch gives 4x Arcane Charge s meaning you can use it to quickly start full-power, sometimes, in easier content, it's better to fire and forget Touch just to get 4x Charges quickly for a quick Arcane Barrage ! Next, you want to ensure your target will live the entire length usually because it does nearly all of its damage after the duration; this is exacerbated by our last Apex talent point, Touch of the Archmage which causes Touch to echo damage for 6-seconds, essentially making Touch a 18-second duration affair. Touch can be talented to cause a damage proc on direct damage via Arcane Echo , proc a Clearcasting via Aegwynn's Technique , conjure Arcane Splinter as , or, as , make Arcane Barrage do more damage during Touch with Sunfury Execution . After all these bolt-on effects, you also must consider that Touch's overall damage output is dependent on your ability to deal damage to your target during Touch's duration. Ultimately, this all adds up to a lot of damage investment over the 18-second period; you'll usually want to use it on the toughest enemy in the pack or the one most likely to kill the group if it doesn't die quickly!

All of that to say, this is a 45-second cooldown, don't sit on it more than a few seconds, especially the Touch that you're not pairing with Arcane Surge .

 Evocation 

 Evocation is very straight forward, simply use it if you're out of mana and can't afford to cast another spell and have no other procs and it will restore all of your mana. Typically, you wouldn't bother with this if Arcane Surge is coming up shortly.

 Arcane Mage Advanced Tips

These tips are more about being a good caster than anything, they're not all Arcane specific much less Mage specific. They have general applicability in World of Warcraft. Remember the mantra ABC: Always Be Casting. More often than not anyone having issues dealing damage they need only look at what they can do to fix their downtime. Below are some tips to help you do that as well as some general Arcane rotational tips.

 Optimizing Damage as Arcane

Some key things to note in general about good gameplay that will make you stand out;
 
Optimize around Arcane Salvo ; try to think about your next few seconds of gameplay, will adds spawn that need to die fast? Will the adds that are up now die soon? Consider saving and not saving around the current conditions - more adds generally means more damage overall and to your main target, thanks to Resonance .

Don't allow yourself to get frazzled with mechanics, when movement is required, try to react quickly and consider your Shimmer path and destination, ensure that you use Stutter Stepping in conjunction with Shimmer to minimize your downtime when handling mechanics.

 Prismatic Barrier is a must-cast defensive. Mages are not as tanky as we used to be, and Barrier spells received a sizable buff to both their quality and to their cast time - they only require 0.5 seconds now to cast, so there's no excuse - you can't deal damage if you're dead!

 Alter Time is a strong defensive, but don't be afraid to also double tap it for mobility in the moment. This can help you keep up with classes that have much better sustained mobility.

Your cooldown window only needs about 18 seconds for and a maximum of 26 seconds for , and 18s for your miniburns; don't hold your cooldowns for too long if you can help it, remember how short the cooldown on Touch of the Magi and Arcane Surge are!
 

 Stutter Stepping

Stutter stepping is the art of efficient movement and is something every caster should master, the below gif explains how it works; you can always find this resource at the Altered Time discord as well.

 The Spellqueue Window

There is a large amount of misinformation out in the internet about what the spellqueue window is and how it works. I hope this short write up will help elaborate on this misunderstood topic.

The spellqueue window is a brief window (default 0.4 seconds long) that exist at the end of casted spells and the global cooldown (GCD) that enables you to press your next button and queue the spell up at the exact point that your current cast or GCD finishes. This allows you to have seamless casting, see this example from one of my logs:

The Arcane Blast s begin exactly where the previous ones end. This minimizes downtime and without spellqueueing we would have gaps in our casting between spells; these gaps would add up overtime and result in significant losses, especially gaps during cooldown windows.

The above is not something people generally disagree with, the spellqueue window prevents gaps in casting, however, where some people make the misunderstanding is on how that specific window works. The mistaken recommendation is that people lower this window to some factor of their ping or as a response to queueing the wrong spell, most common are people lowering it to 0.1-0.2 seconds. The issue with this is that most people do not spam keys 5-10 times a second, which is what lowering the queue window to this point would require to maintain the same seamless benefit, while the 0.4 second default only requires 3 presses per second.

If this were the only issue and was solved by simply hitting buttons faster, I would say 'go for it' if you can sustain that during playtime, however, there is no benefit to lowering the window for the reasons above and so there is only risk here. The spellqueue window can be overwritten up until the spell that is queued begins; this means that lowering it because of ping or wrong spell queueing would be solved by simply just queueing the spell correctly as soon as possible. What is instead happening is that people are not queueing their spells, resulting in a gap of time where they then queue up the 'correct' feeling spell. The spellqueue window was added to the game to combat lag issues, the idea that people are trying to remove its value because of lag issues is comedy, and the people who will insist that it helps them not cast the wrong spells, especially during high haste, are just hitting the wrong buttons and breaking their queue to solve the issue rather than training themselves to hit the right button sooner.

Ultimately, this matters less for specializations that are resource starved or healers or tanks where the 'right' button press is often more important than uptime, it also matters less for the players at the top levels of gameplay, but it matters a lot for the vast majority of dps that we have seamless and consistent uptime. For this reason, I would highly recommend you leave this at the default 0.4 second value. I hope this explanation helps, but ultimately the real takeaway from this is that you should attempte to always have spells queued up properly for maximum uptime.

You can reset your spellqueue back to 400 with the code below, but be mindful that some addons will misguidedly set this lower for you.

/console SpellQueueWindow 400

Evocation is not worth using if Arcane Surge is about to come off cooldown, make sure you're not wasting your time channeling this just to spend the mana with Surge, use it for more max Arcane Charge buffed Arcane Blast and Arcane Pulse.

It really is this simple, Arcane Orb with Orb Mastery talented hits hard, but it's not just the Orbs themselves, it generates Arcane Salvo faster than Arcane Missiles, while also producing a bunch of Arcane Splinters. 

Tips:
- To avoid overcapping Arcane Orb charges, you can send one at the start of the pull without Clearcasting or if you're about to cap on charges.
- Be careful about where you aim, Orb can be a sensitive spell at times and occasionally will fall through floors or get hung up on obstacles in the terrain. Occasionally, these will just have to be learned through trial and error unfortunately, however many issues can be avoided by just being considerate and deliberate in your aim.
- Arcane Orb gives 6 Arcane Salvo stacks, plus additional chances per Splinter for more. It's a good practice to avoid overcapping Salvo when possible.
- When you are against 4 or more enemies, you can use Arcane Orb with Clearcasting even if you didn't just use Barrage to get Salvo stacks quicker.

Currently, the talents Intuition from the spec tree, Polished Focus from the ]Spellslinger tree reinforce casting Arcane Barrage when you have maximum stacks of Arcane Salvo.

Tips:
- If Touch of the Magi is coming off cooldown in the next 4-5s, try to hold off on this if you can.
- If you are playing the Orb Barrage talent, you do not necessarily need to build up Arcane Charge s for this line.
- It is also a good practice to Arcane Barrage if you have 15 or more Salvo stacks and are on the last global of Arcane Surge or Touch of the Magi.
- It is also a best practice, when specced into Arcane Pulse to also Barrage if you have less than 7 Arcane Salvo stacks, are not in cooldowns, and didn't cast an Orb after Barrage from the above condition. This is because of the tax Pulse puts on our Mana and you're basically hoping for the chance of getting an Orb Barrage proc.

Tips:
- In AOE, if you have a single target you want to eliminate as a priority over other targets, you should use Arcane Blast instead for filler.
- You can use this as an Arcane Charge generator since Reverberate will make it more efficient at building Charges.

Currently, the talents Intuition from the spec tree, Polished Focus from the ]Spellslinger tree reinforce casting Arcane Barrage when you have maximum stacks of Arcane Salvo.

Tips:
- If Touch of the Magi is coming off cooldown in the next ~4s, try to hold off for Touch.
- If you are playing the Orb Barrage talent, you do not necessarily need to build up Arcane Charge s for this line.

Tips:
- This is really about not overcapping Arcane Salvo, if you're over 14 Salvo, it's a good practice to just keep going til 20, then Barrage.
- If Touch of the Magi is coming off cooldown in the next ~4s, try to hold off on this if you can.

Tips:
- Clipping does not seem to be worthwhile currently.
- To reduce overcapping, cast Arcane Missiles only if you have less than 15 Arcane Salvo stacks, less than 10 if you have Overpowered Missiles up.

Overpowered Missiles gives nearly full Arcane Salvo stacks, so it's a good practice to clear the stacks you have before your spend it. No need to do this if you don't have any Arcane Salvo stacks.

Tips:
- Clipping does not seem to be worthwhile currently. However, if you are at certain haste thresholds, this particular cast can be valuable to clip if it will result in more Arcane Barrages during Arcane Soul.
- Prior to Arcane Soul, you should try to find a way to spend your Clearcasting procs, cast Arcane Barrage prior to Arcane Soul; this sounds confusing at first, but you build a rhythm of dumping some Arcane Missiles, using Touch of the Magi, dropping a huge Arcane Barrage, then build back up for Arcane Soul.

Due to the hero talent Sunfury Execution and our Apex talent Touch of the Archmage, we will always try to Arcane Barrage while Touch of the Magi is active on our target to leverage this ability. For Sunfury this also means using Barrage after Touch, not before like Spellslinger.

Currently, the talent Intuition from the spec tree reinforces casting Arcane Barrage when you have maximum stacks of Arcane Salvo, but that is juxtaposed against getting fast Salvo and Arcane Charge generation from Missiles.

A common question here is, why 19? Really a lot of values work here, it could just as easily be 18 ,19, or 20. The idea is that you want to maximize your potential Meteorites from Glorious Incandescence, but also once you get close enough to Intuition, just go for it.

Tips:
- If Touch of the Magi or Arcane Surge is coming off cooldown in the next ~4s, try to hold off on this if you can, if you get procs like Overpowered Missiles or multiple Clearcasting procs you can bend this rule a bit for Sunfury.
- The best results here will come from weaving Arcane Blast/Pulse in to maximize Meteorite generation before casting Arcane Barrage with Clearcasting, this hold strue for . This means that if you get a Clearcasting proc at 4 stacks, you would Blast/Pulse once to get to 6 stacks, then Barrage to get a Meteorite; then use Missiles to regenerate Charges and Salvo. Likewise, if you were at 10, Blast/Pulse to get to 12 and so on.

Tips:
- Clipping does not seem to be worthwhile currently.
- To reduce overcapping, cast Arcane Missiles only if you have less than 15 Arcane Salvo stacks, less than 10 if you have Overpowered Missiles.

I'm a bit unsure about how exactly the 4 vs 5 AB casts with Harmonic Echo works, so I want to share my understanding of the mechanics and see if it tracks. 

Normally we can queue the big Barr with the 5th AB, because since they both "release" simultaneously, they both benefit from the final stack of Radiant Spark. This lets us get a sort of 2 for 1 with the final charge, increasing damage in single target. 
The Harmonic Echo effect causes a 25% aoe echo to spells that LAND while the debuff is active, so if we cast the 5th AB with a queued Barr, they will still both benefit from the Radiant Spark damage increase, but only the 5th AB will cause the echo, since the debuff is gone by the time the Barr lands.
